html:
The Brahmo Samaj is a Hindu reform movement founded in Calcutta in 1828 by Ram Mohan Roy and Dwarkanath Tagore. It was a driving force of the Bengal Renaissance.

It taught worship of one formless God, based on reason and on the Upanishads. It rejected idol worship, priestly ritual and caste, and campaigned for women's education and for widows' right to remarry.

The movement had three main phases:

  • After Roy's death, Debendranath Tagore, father of Rabindranath, revived it in the 1840s and gave it a creed and a form of worship.
  • In 1866 Keshub Chandra Sen led a more radical group away, open to Christian ideas and to social reform.
  • In 1878 many left Keshub after he married his young daughter to a prince, and formed the Sadharan Brahmo Samaj.

It never had many members. Its weight lay in who joined: the families that led Bengal's writing, science and politics in the late 1800s. Its ideas fed into later movements such as the Arya Samaj and into the reforms that ended the ban on widow remarriage.
sum: The Brahmo Samaj is a Hindu reform movement founded in Calcutta in 1828 by Ram Mohan Roy and Dwarkanath Tagore. It was a driving force of the Bengal Renaissance.
